title: Linked list: reverse a sublist
summary: Reverse positions left..right (1-based) of a linked list in one pass. A dummy head covers left = 1; flip next pointers inside the range, then reconnect both ends. O(n), O(1) space. The Node class is shown, not typed.
code: # Flip next pointers inside the range, then reconnect both ends.
triggers: reverse all or part of a linked list in place
reorder nodes by rewiring next pointers, without copying values
prompts: A playlist is stored as a chain of tracks, each pointing to the next. Reverse the order of tracks 3 through 7 in place.
A train's carriages are coupled one to the next. Turn around a run of consecutive carriages in the middle while the rest of the train stays attached.
invariant: previous heads the already-reversed part of the range, current is the next node to flip, and before.next is still the range's original first node.
mantra: Save next, point back, step forward; then reconnect both ends.
pitfalls: Save current.next before overwriting it, or the rest of the list is lost.
Without a dummy head, reversing from position 1 needs a special case.
After the loop, before.next is the range's old first node and now its last: point it at current.

anchors.name: Reverse Linked List
anchors.trick: left = 1 and right = n: only the three-line flip remains.

mutations.explanation: Starts one node too far along: the range shifts right by one, so the head can never be reversed.
